title: Monochromatic triangle-tilings in dense graphs without large independent sets
summary: Given two graphs $H$ and $G$, an $H$-tiling is a family of vertex-disjoint copies of $H$ in $G$. A perfect $H$-tiling covers all vertices of $G$. The Corradi-Hajnal theorem (1963) states that an $n$-vertex graph $G$ with minimum degree $δ(G)\ge 2n/3$ contains a perfect triangle-tiling. For an $n$-vertex graph $G$ with independence number $α(G)=o(n)$, Balogh, Molla and Sharifzadeh (Random Structures & Algorithms, 2016) showed that a minimum degree of $(\frac12+o(1))n$ forces a perfect triangle-tiling.
